tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with 'Use this skill when a user asks to reduce, review, audit, or optimize AWS Config spend' — clear imperative phrasing. It focuses on user intent (reducing cost, understanding a bill spike) and lists many explicit trigger phrases/contexts a user might use ('why is my AWS Config bill so high', 'my configuration item count spiked', etc.), covering cases where the user doesn't name the domain directly. It is a single dense but bounded paragraph, and while lengthy, it stays focused on describing scope/triggers rather than internals, with only a brief closing clause summarizing the mechanism.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user asks to reduce, review, audit, or optimize AWS Config spend, or reports an unexpected AWS Config cost or configuration-item increase. Activate on requests like "why is my AWS Config bill so high", "reduce Config costs"...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is focused on AWS Config-specific domain knowledge (billing model, CI drivers, opportunity checks) rather than general concepts the agent already knows. It stays concise, deferring deep detail to reference files.
tests.evidence: Configuration items (CIs) are the dominant cost driver — billed per CI recorded.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body summarizes billing essentials briefly and pushes detailed tables, API lists, and check definitions to references/ files. Decision-tree detail (conformance-pack overlap) is only briefly summarized in body with pointer to reference for full detail.
tests.evidence: For the full charge table, per-mode pricing, and the high-churn reasoning the checks rely on, load [references/billing-model.md](references/billing-model.md)

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All three reference files are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link specifies a clear condition or purpose for loading, e.g. deciding continuous vs daily, or performing the eight opportunity checks.
tests.evidence: load [references/billing-model.md](references/billing-model.md) when you need to decide whether continuous or daily is cheaper for a resource type, or to explain a charge.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths from the skill root in the correct format.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/compliance-sensitive operations (read-only boundaries, conformance-pack overlap) are prescriptive with explicit warnings, while flexible analysis steps (like which severity to assign) leave room for judgment with explained rationale.
tests.evidence: Never recommend dropping recording below the organization's audit requirements... Do not recommend merging them into a union pack, or deleting one, unless the customer confirms

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Cost signal collection specifies a clear preferred default (Cost Explorer) with fallbacks explicitly labeled as such.
tests.evidence: Prefer Cost Explorer as the dollar signal, use Athena (or `GetDiscoveredResourceCounts` as an approximate fallback) for CI-driver attribution

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable procedure (scope, inventory, cost signals, analysis, validation, report) applicable to any AWS Config cost review, not a one-off instance-specific declaration.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Identify target scope. Ask the user which accounts and Regions to review...

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has a dedicated 'Known Quirks' section documenting non-obvious, environment-specific facts (Control Tower recorder resets, GetDiscoveredResourceCounts limitations, conformance pack overlap intentionality).
tests.evidence: In Control Tower / Organizations environments, recorder settings may be centrally managed and reset on account provisioning

tests.name: Validation loops
